Hi Jane / Carlos,

Thanks again for your time earlier — really appreciate the thoughtful questions. Quick recap from our demo and suggested next steps so you have everything in one place: 

- Recap: We walked through Redwood Hosted API (low-friction onboarding), the model catalog, streaming responses, and basic observability. You mentioned primary concerns: throughput for inference (50 req/s target), latency SLOs (~200-500ms), and PHI/data residency requirements.

- Questions for you (to help us recommend the right path):
  1) Is PHI involved in this evaluation (yes/no)? If yes, will you require a BAA or on-prem/private deployment?
  2) Can you confirm the expected average tokens per request (you mentioned ~6k tokens earlier) and concurrency pattern (burst vs steady)?
  3) Any strict data residency or retention policies (US-only, EU-only, retention <30 days, etc.)?

- Quick wins we can do now:
  • I can provision eval API keys for Hosted and a short-lived Dedicated sandbox if you want to emulate steady 50 rps.
  • Dev will send a quickstart CURL + sample streaming and non-streaming requests.
  • I attached our quickstart guide and a short evaluation checklist (one-pager) to make the POC smooth.

Next steps: if you can reply with answers to the three questions above, we’ll send an evaluation plan and recommended configuration (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private). I’ve CC’d Dev who can jump on a technical deep-dive once you’re ready. Would you be open to a 30-min follow-up later this week?

Thanks,
Marissa

Subject: Re: Hosted API eval follow-up — quickstart, endpoints, and rate limits

Marissa — thanks for the recap and attachments. A few clarifications before we schedule the next call: 

On PHI/data: Yes, our workload will process PHI. We will need a BAA and US-only data residency for at least the evaluation period.

On throughput/latency: The 50 req/s (steady-state) was a peak target — typical day traffic is more bursty, but we need the infra to handle sustained bursts of ~50 rps for short windows. Average payload is ~4–6k tokens per request depending on use case. Latency target is as low as possible; <500ms would be ideal but 200–500ms is our target range for user-facing flows.

Questions we need answered before proceeding: 
1) Can Hosted API meet sustained 50 rps with ~6k tokens without unacceptable latency?
2) What are the default rate limits on Hosted API and how do those scale (per-key, per-account)?
3) What does data retention look like for Hosted (default retention window, options to opt-out / disable storage)?
4) Can you provide a trial API key and a quick guide for running the first few requests (curl example + streaming)?

If Hosted won’t reliably meet the SLOs we’ll need to talk Dedicated capacity or Private VPC. Happy to hop on another call once we have these details — does tomorrow morning 10am PT work?

Thanks,
Jane Miller
Head of Product | AtlasCare
jane.miller@atlascare.com

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Miller <jane.miller@atlascare.com>, Carlos Ruiz <carlos.ruiz@atlascare.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-01T18:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API eval follow-up — quickstart, endpoints, and rate limits

Hi Jane — Dev here (Solutions Eng) — quick technical answers and a couple of practical notes. I’ll keep this focused so you can decide if Hosted is viable for your eval: 

1) Throughput & latency (Hosted):
   - Hosted can handle bursts but there are two dimensions: per-API-key rate limits and overall account pool behavior. Default Hosted limits: ~300 requests/minute per key and soft concurrent request limits that vary by model. Those defaults are conservative for new accounts.
   - For 50 rps sustained with ~6k tokens, we typically recommend Dedicated capacity for predictable latency and cost. However, for an evaluation you can: 
     a) use a higher-rate eval key (we can temporarily raise limits and enable burst capacity), or
     b) run a short Dedicated sandbox (reserved pool) to validate steady-state latency.
   - Typical latency numbers (observed): small requests return ~80–200ms on good hardware; large 6k-token requests are dominated by model compute and will be higher (200–800ms depending on model). We can recommend specific model/quantization profiles to improve latency.

2) Rate limits & scaling:
   - We expose per-key rate limits and an account-level pool. For production at 50 rps we usually provision a Dedicated pool sized for your token throughput and SLO. For Hosted evaluations we can temporarily elevate your per-key RPM and enable additional concurrency for a defined test window.

3) Data retention & compliance:
   - Hosted default: request/response payloads are retained for 30 days for debugging and quality monitoring; you can opt-out of retention for a given eval key. Redwood is SOC 2 Type II compliant; we also support BAAs for healthcare customers. Data residency: we can ensure US-only regions for your evaluation.

4) Quickstart samples (short):
Non-streaming example:

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"model":"open-compat-small","input":"Summarize patient visit notes","max_tokens":6000}'

Streaming (SSE) example:

curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"model":"open-compat-small","input":"Summarize patient visit notes","stream":true}'
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate/stream

Endpoints:
  - Text generation: POST /v1/generate (streaming /v1/generate/stream)
  - Chat: POST /v1/chat (streaming /v1/chat/stream)
  - Embeddings: POST /v1/embeddings
  - Metadata & usage: GET /v1/usage, GET /v1/keys

Notes on recommended eval approach:
  - If you want to validate production SLOs, we can spin up a short Dedicated sandbox for 48–72 hours pre-configured for your 50 rps target. That gives deterministic latency and a realistic cost profile.
  - If you prefer to start with Hosted, we’ll raise your limits for the test window and provide an eval key with retention disabled on request.

I’ll attach a short checklist and the quickstart (Marissa included them already) and can run a load test with you once you confirm the test window. If helpful, I’m free for a 30-min technical session tomorrow 11am PT.

—Dev
